title: Exclude common image or kernel lines from the diagonal pair (no κ)
body:
Prove that a common image line or a common kernel line can never realise the width-two diagonal-pair target, at any word length and over any field, and that at most two calls never suffice under the target hypotheses of #6097.

## Result and claim type

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. No new κ, no supplier, no selected-frontier change.

Setting: the rank-one-idempotent register model of Wentao Li's #4089, as used by Nick Petalas's #6038, Josie Elliston's #6048/#6137 and JoyboyBrian's #6097. For a field `F`, a group `G`, labels `L` and a rank-one idempotent `N ∈ M₂(F)`, a call is `D_N(g) = (I−N) + [g]N`.

**Theorem 1.** Let `N₁,…,N_k` be rank-one idempotents that share a common image line, or share a common kernel line. Then for every labels and every `k ≥ 0`, the product `∏ D_{N_i}(g_i)` is never `diag([a],[b])` with `a ≠ e ≠ b`. This holds over every field and every group.

Proof sketch: with a common image line, `N_i = u v_iᵀ` and `v_iᵀu = 1`, so `N_iN_j = N_j`. Every subset product collapses to its last projector, and the whole product is `I + u wᵀ` with `u` a field vector and `w` over `F[G]`. Hence `det(P−I) = 0`. For `a ≠ b` the element `([a]−1)([b]−1)` is nonzero in `F[G]` over every field, so a diagonal pair with distinct targets is impossible. The common-kernel case is the transpose argument.

**Corollary.** Any word attaining `diag([a],[b])` with `a ≠ b`, neither target a product of at most two labels, must contain two projectors with distinct image lines and two with distinct kernel lines. In particular no family with a single image line, a single kernel line or one repeated projector can attain the pair at any length.

**Theorem 2.** Over every field and group, no product of at most two calls equals `diag([a],[b])` when `a ≠ b` and neither target is a product of at most two labels. Without the length hypothesis two calls do suffice: `D_{E00}(x) D_{E11}(y) = diag([x],[y])`.

This is the field/width scope left open by Open next question 2 of JoyboyBrian's #6097 ("does the six-call floor extend to odd characteristic or F4?", blocked by "even pairing is specific to F2"). It answers that question only in part: a whole family of candidate counterexamples is removed at every length and field, and lengths 0–2 are removed. The general `F4`, `F5`, odd-characteristic and larger-width six-call floors remain open.

## Evidence and reproduction

Package: `research/diagonal-pair-line-separation/` (`README.md`, `PROOF.md`, `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `VERIFY.json`, `verify.py`).

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/diagonal-pair-line-separation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -B research/diagonal-pair-line-separation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/diagonal-pair-line-separation
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/diagonal-pair-line-separation --check-source-history
```

`verify.py` is standard-library only, about 0.7 s per run, and prints one line beginning `PASS_DIAGONAL_PAIR_LINE_SEPARATION`. It builds each field from its arithmetic, derives the rank-one idempotent inventory from `N² = N` and `tr(N) = 1`, and checks by exact arithmetic:

- inventories `q(q+1) = 6, 12, 20, 30` over `F2, F3, F4, F5`;
- all `24 / 72 / 160 / 300` ordered same-image and same-kernel pairs satisfy the collapse `N_iN_j = N_j` or its transpose;
- `7,812 / 71,736 / 43,400 / 123,960` nonempty subset products collapse to the last or first projector;
- the determinant of `P−I` vanishes for all `372 / 2,904 / 3,400 / 9,360` enumerated same-line tuples at lengths up to 5 over `F2, F3` and up to 4 over `F4, F5`, computed by exact expansion in the group algebra of the free abelian group on the call positions;
- the two-call diagonal-forcing step for every projector over each field;
- the positive control `D_{E00}(x)³ D_{E11}(y)³ = diag([x³],[y³])` with its four predicted coefficients, and the mixed-line negative control `D_{E00}(x) D_{E11}(y)` with a nonzero determinant.

The free abelian group is a commutative instance, which is what the rank argument uses. Checks raise explicit exceptions, so `-O` does not disable them.

Local status: both registered VERIFY commands, `scripts/research_package.py` and `scripts/check_research_commit.py --check-source-history` pass at head `2c2dad2058a4f01485214b7437b3e8b8d4d8f57c`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Theorems 1 and 2 only. Nothing here bounds tuples with two or more image lines, which is where any counterexample must live.
- Theorem 2 is a written argument; only its diagonal-forcing step is machine checked.
- The finite enumeration corroborates the collapse and the determinant identity. It is not a proof kernel and not a complete tuple census.
- The general `F4`, `F5`, odd-characteristic and larger-width six-call floors are not decided.
- No native tariff, compiler, supplier or multiplication bound is inferred.

## Related open work

No open PR was found that studies the same diagonal-pair line separation. The own-open-PR check at head `2c2dad2058a4f01485214b7437b3e8b8d4d8f57c` also found none from this account on this object; the nearest open one, #7213, proves an exact diagonal-rank cost in a different group-gate model, and no number is compared with it. The source question is JoyboyBrian's merged #6097; Josie Elliston's merged #6048/#6137 supply the width-two framing and the four-call floor; Nick Petalas's merged #6609 supplies a related symmetry quotient of the same projector domain and is cited as related work, not used as a step. No number in this PR depends on another open PR.

## Open next questions

1. Does the six-call floor hold over `F4`? The remaining search is the `267,072` five-call representatives of #6609 restricted to tuples with at least two image lines and two kernel lines.
2. Same for `F5` and general odd characteristic, where the even-pairing argument of #6097 has no direct analogue.
3. Does the line-exclusion argument extend to rank-one idempotents in `M_d(F)` at widths above two, where the same collapse holds but the target is a `d`-fold diagonal?
